  • Benefits derived from the policy were modest.
Notes: derive from 源自；derivation 派生/推导。
SynonymDistinction: obtain 泛指‘获得’；derive 强调‘从源头推导/得出’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Four pillars underpin the theory.
  • Strong institutions underpin economic growth.
  • The claim is underpinned by solid data.
Notes: 比喻‘打下基础’；名词 underpinning。
SynonymDistinction: support 泛‘支持’；underpin 强调‘从根基上支撑’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Trade agreements facilitate exchange.
  • The app facilitates communication across teams.
  • Good design facilitates learning.
Notes: 不以‘人’作宾语（不说 facilitate sb.）；名词 facility 设施。
SynonymDistinction: ease 使‘更容易’；facilitate 较正式‘促成/提供便利’。

Definition: 义1. 有益于…的；促成…的
Examples:
义1:
  • A quiet room is conducive to study.
  • The climate is conducive to outdoor life.
  • This culture is not conducive to frank debate.
Notes: 常接 to + 名词/动名词；反义 detrimental（有害的）。
SynonymDistinction: favourable 有利；conducive 强调‘有助于产生某结果的环境条件’。

Definition: 义1. 仔细审查（美 scrutinize）
Examples:
义1:
  • Reviewers scrutinised every claim.
  • We must scrutinise the assumptions closely.
  • The data were scrutinised for errors.
Notes: 名词 scrutiny 审查；形容‘细致检查’。
SynonymDistinction: examine 一般‘检查’；scrutinise 强调‘逐字逐句地仔细审查’。

Definition: 义1. 把…归因于（attribute A to B）
Examples:
义1:
  • She attributed the drop to poor policy.
  • The effect is attributed to climate change.
  • We attribute the result to random chance.
Notes: 注意重音：动词 /əˈtrɪbjuːt/，名词 /ˈætrɪbjuːt/‘特质’。
SynonymDistinction: ascribe 也‘归于’，常偏主观；attribute 更常用于因果归因。

Examples:
义1:
  • Notwithstanding the risks, they proceeded.
  • The law applies, difficulties notwithstanding.
  • His objections notwithstanding, the plan passed.
Notes: 正式，位置灵活（可置句首/句末/名词后）；= despite。
SynonymDistinction: despite 最常用；notwithstanding 更正式且位置灵活。

Examples:
义1:
  • The sample comprises 500 households.
  • The committee is comprised of experts.
  • The book comprises three parts.
Notes: 不用被动进行时‘comprising of’是错的；正确 comprise / be comprised of。
SynonymDistinction: consist of 与 comprise 同义但 comprise 语气更正式；include 不一定穷尽。

Definition: 义1. 转喻（以相关物代本体）
Examples:
义1:
  • ‘The crown’ is a metonymy for the monarchy.
  • ‘The pen is mightier than the sword’ uses metonymy.
  • Wall Street is a metonymy for finance.
Notes: 与 metaphor 不同：metonymy 是‘相关替换’，非‘类比’。
SynonymDistinction: synecdoche 以部分代整体（如 wheels 代 car）；metonymy 以相关物代（crown 代 king）。

Examples:
义1:
  • Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets.
  • The sonnet follows a strict rhyme scheme.
  • She composed a Petrarchan sonnet.
Notes: Shakespearean (ABAB CDCD EFEF GG) / Petrarchan 两种韵式。

Examples:
义1:
  • Tennyson's elegy honoured his friend.
  • The elegy mourns a lost world.
  • She wrote an elegy for the fallen city.
Notes: 悼亡之作；形容词 elegiac；与 eulogy（颂词）不同。
SynonymDistinction: eulogy 是‘赞颂词’；elegy 是‘哀悼诗’。

Definition: 义1. 田园的（牧歌体裁）
Examples:
义1:
  • The play has a pastoral setting.
  • Pastoral poems idealise rural life.
  • He painted a pastoral of shepherds and streams.
Notes: 题材：乡村/牧人理想化；名词 a pastoral 田园诗/画。
SynonymDistinction: bucolic 乡村的；pastoral 特指‘牧歌式理想化乡村’；idyllic 偏‘恬静美好’。

Definition: 义1. 无韵诗（素体诗，不押韵的抑扬格五音步）
Examples:
义1:
  • Much of Hamlet is written in blank verse.
  • Milton's Paradise Lost uses blank verse.
  • Blank verse suits the rhythms of speech.
Notes: = unrhymed iambic pentameter；与 free verse 自由诗不同。
SynonymDistinction: free verse 完全自由无格律；blank verse 有格律但不押韵。

Examples:
义1:
  • The play is a tragicomedy of misunderstanding.
  • Waiting for Godot blends farce and tragicomedy.
  • Her novel is a quiet tragicomedy of family life.
Notes: 混合悲剧与喜剧元素；形容词 tragicomic。

Definition: 义1. （戏剧）机械降神；突兀解困
Examples:
义1:
  • The rescue felt like a deus ex machina.
  • Critics mocked the deus ex machina ending.
  • Avoid a deus ex machina in your plot.
Notes: 原指古希腊舞台机关送神解围；今指‘生硬强行收尾’。

Definition: 义1. 首语重复（句首重复以加强）
Examples:
义1:
  • ‘I have a dream’ uses anaphora.
  • Anaphora opens each stanza with ‘We shall’.
  • The speech gains force from anaphora.
Notes: 修辞格；与 epistrophe（尾语重复）相对。

Definition: 义1. 格律；韵律（美 meter）
Examples:
义1:
  • The metre is iambic pentameter.
  • He scanned the line for its metre.
  • Free verse abandons regular metre.
Notes: 韵律单位；scan 析韵律；与 rhythm 不同，metre 是规则格律。
SynonymDistinction: rhythm 泛指节奏；metre 是‘系统化格律’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The novel achieves verisimilitude through detail.
  • Realism prizes verisimilitude over fantasy.
  • The film's verisimilitude impressed critics.
Notes: ‘the appearance of being true’；形容词 verisimilar。
SynonymDistinction: authenticity 真实（确实真）；verisimilitude 是‘看起来像真的’。

Definition: 义1. 时代错误（置于错误年代的事物）
Examples:
义1:
  • A wristwatch in a Roman film is an anachronism.
  • The clock was an anachronism in the medieval scene.
  • Calling them ‘nations’ is a historical anachronism.
Notes: 形容词 anachronistic；常用于批评年代错置。

Examples:
义1:
  • The dispute ended in litigation.
  • Litigation can take years and drain funds.
  • They settled to avoid litigation.
Notes: 动词 litigate；litigious 好诉讼的。
SynonymDistinction: lawsuit 指具体‘一案’；litigation 泛指‘诉讼过程/行为’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The defendant pleaded not guilty.
  • The defendant was acquitted for lack of evidence.
  • Witnesses testified against the defendant.
Notes: 民事诉讼 plaintiff 原告；刑事 prosecution 检方。
SynonymDistinction: accused 偏刑事‘被指控者’；defendant 通用‘被告’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The ruling set a dangerous precedent.
  • Decisions follow established precedent.
  • There is no precedent for such a case.
Notes: stare decisis 遵循先例；binding / persuasive precedent。
SynonymDistinction: example 普通例子；precedent 法律‘可援引的先例’。

Definition: 义1. 公正的；不偏不倚的
Examples:
义1:
  • The judge must remain impartial.
  • An impartial jury is essential to fairness.
  • The mediator was wholly impartial.
Notes: 名词 impartiality；与 neutral 近义但更正式。
SynonymDistinction: neutral 中立；impartial 强调‘无偏私、公正裁决’。

Examples:
义1:
  • He won his London constituency.
  • The policy pleases her rural constituency.
  • MPs represent their constituencies in parliament.
Notes: 议员 constituency MP；也泛指‘支持群体’。
SynonymDistinction: district 地理选区；electorate 全体选民；constituency 二者皆可。

Examples:
义1:
  • A coalition formed after the hung election.
  • The coalition collapsed within a year.
  • They built a coalition of civil-society groups.
Notes: coalition government 联合政府；动词 coalesce 联合。
SynonymDistinction: alliance 泛指联盟；coalition 多指‘为执政/行动临时结成的联合’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The policy reflects a free-market ideology.
  • Competing ideologies shaped the century.
  • He rejected all political ideology.
Notes: ideological 意识形态的；-ism 常表具体思潮。
SynonymDistinction: doctrine 教义/学说；ideology 更宽‘一套政治社会信念体系’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The country slid into autocracy.
  • Autocracy concentrates power in one ruler.
  • They opposed the return to autocracy.
Notes: autocrat 独裁者；对比 democracy / theocracy。
SynonymDistinction: dictatorship 强调‘独裁者个人统治’；autocracy 泛指‘集权政体’。

Examples:
义1:
  • France refused to extradite the suspect.
  • The treaty allows us to extradite fugitives.
  • He was extradited to stand trial abroad.
Notes: 名词 extradition；extradite sb. to...

Examples:
义1:
  • The king granted a general amnesty.
  • Amnesty was offered to defectors.
  • They demanded amnesty for political prisoners.
Notes: 与 pardon（特赦个别人）不同；amnesty 多针对群体。
SynonymDistinction: pardon 特赦个人；amnesty 对一类人的‘大赦’。

Definition: 义1. 传染性的（接触传播）
Examples:
义1:
  • The flu is highly contagious.
  • Keep contagious children home.
  • Yawning is surprisingly contagious.
Notes: 与 infectious 区别：contagious 多经接触；infectious 可经空气/体液，也喻‘有感染力’。
SynonymDistinction: infectious 空气/体液传播或‘有感染力’；contagious 接触传播。

Examples:
义1:
  • She has an allergy to nuts.
  • The rash was an allergic reaction.
  • Peanut allergy can be life-threatening.
Notes: 形容词 allergic；allergen 过敏原。

Examples:
义1:
  • He suffered a fractured wrist.
  • The bone fractured on impact.
  • The fracture healed in six weeks.
Notes: compound fracture 开放性骨折；fissure 裂纹。
SynonymDistinction: break 口语‘断’；fracture 医学‘骨折/裂’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The trial used a placebo control.
  • The pill was a inert placebo.
  • Some felt better on placebo alone.
Notes: placebo effect 安慰剂效应；inert 无药效的。

Examples:
义1:
  • He had a kidney transplant.
  • Doctors transplanted the liver.
  • The transplanted organ was rejected.
Notes: organ transplant 器官移植；reject 排异。

Examples:
义1:
  • The doctor gave a mild sedative.
  • Sedatives calm the nervous system.
  • He was drowsy from the sedative.
Notes: 与 stimulant（兴奋剂）反义；sedate 使镇静。
SynonymDistinction: tranquilliser 安定剂；sedative 泛指镇静剂。

Examples:
义1:
  • The surgeon made a small incision.
  • The incision healed without infection.
  • The incision was closed with sutures.
Notes: 动词 incise；反义 suture/stitch 缝合。
SynonymDistinction: cut 普通切；incision 医学‘手术切口’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Her heart palpitated with fear.
  • Caffeine made his heart palpitate.
  • The heart palpitated irregularly.
Notes: palpitations 心悸（症状）；与 beat 不同，指‘异常快/乱跳’。

Examples:
义1:
  • We grilled the asparagus with oil.
  • Asparagus is in season in spring.
  • She trimmed the woody ends of the asparagus.
Notes: 蔬菜；woody end 老根需去。

Examples:
义1:
  • Sauté the onions until translucent.
  • She sautéed the mushrooms in butter.
  • Sauté the garlic briefly, don't burn it.
Notes: 法文；= pan-fry lightly；名词 a sauté。
SynonymDistinction: fry 泛指煎炸；sauté 强调‘少油快火嫩煎’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Marinate the chicken overnight.
  • The beef marinated in wine and herbs.
  • Let it marinate at least two hours.
Notes: marinade 腌料；也写作 marine。
SynonymDistinction: cure 风干/盐制保存；marinate 用液料浸泡入味。

Definition: 义1. 鲜味（第五种基本味）
Examples:
义1:
  • Mushrooms add umami to the dish.
  • Soy sauce is rich in umami.
  • Umami balances sweetness and acid.
Notes: 日语‘うま味’；第五味觉，与 sweet/sour/salty/bitter 并列。
SynonymDistinction: savouriness 英式‘咸鲜’；umami 专指‘鲜味’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The pastry was light and flaky.
  • She rolled the pastry thin.
  • French pastries lined the window.
Notes: flaky 起酥；与 pasta（面团/意面）不同。
SynonymDistinction: dough 生面团；pastry 指‘油酥类糕点’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The broth simmered for hours.
  • Skim the broth before serving.
  • A clear broth started the meal.
Notes: broth 清汤；stock 高汤（更浓）；bouillon 块汤。
SynonymDistinction: stock 熬制的浓高汤；broth 较稀的汤；soup 成品汤。

Definition: 义1. 单宁（茶/酒中的涩味物质）
Examples:
义1:
  • The red wine's tannin dried the mouth.
  • Tannin gives tea its astringency.
  • Young wines are high in tannin.
Notes: astringent 涩；也用于皮革鞣制。

Examples:
义1:
  • Yeast ferments the sugar into alcohol.
  • The cabbage fermented into sauerkraut.
  • Let the dough ferment overnight.
Notes: 名词 fermentation；fermented 发酵的（酸奶/酒/泡菜）。
SynonymDistinction: leaven 用酵母发（面团）；ferment 广义‘发酵（含酒/乳/菜）’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Garnish the soup with herbs.
  • A lemon wedge garnished the plate.
  • Parsley is a common garnish.
Notes: 名词‘装饰配菜’；与 decorate 近但专指食物。
SynonymDistinction: decorate 泛指装饰；garnish 专指‘菜肴点缀’。

Examples:
义1:
  • French cuisine is rich and buttery.
  • The region boasts a unique cuisine.
  • She trained in classic cuisine.
Notes: 表‘某国/地烹饪’；也指厨房（设备）。
SynonymDistinction: cooking 烹饪行为；cuisine 指‘体系化的菜系’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The broth was umami-laden and deep.
  • Aged cheese is umami-laden.
  • The sauce turned umami-laden with miso.
Notes: -laden 充满…的；描述鲜味浓。

Definition: 义1. 剁碎；肉末（美 ground meat）
Examples:
义1:
  • Mince the garlic finely.
  • She bought beef mince for the sauce.
  • He minced the herbs with a knife.
Notes: 英 mince / 美 ground；mincemeat 果脯馅（非肉）。
SynonymDistinction: chop 切块；mince/grind 剁/磨成末。

Definition: 义1. 熬成焦糖；炒糖色
Examples:
义1:
  • Caramelise the sugar slowly.
  • Onions caramelise to a golden brown.
  • The sauce caramelised at the edges.
Notes: 美 caramelize；焦糖化反应。

Definition: 义1. 清秀的；好看的（旧式/文雅）
Examples:
义1:
  • A comely village maid appeared.
  • He described her as comely and kind.
  • The comely face hid a sharp mind.
Notes: 较 archaic，现多用于文学；近 pretty 但更端庄。
SynonymDistinction: pretty 日常漂亮；comely 文雅‘清秀端庄’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The willowy model glided in.
  • She had a willowy, graceful figure.
  • A willowy dancer bent like a reed.
Notes: 喻 like a willow 柳树般柔韧；tall and slender。
SynonymDistinction: slender 苗条；willowy 强调‘高挑且柔韧如柳’。

Definition: 义1. （女性）庄重丰腴的；主妇气的
Examples:
义1:
  • She wore a matronly dress.
  • A matronly figure supervised the hall.
  • The matronly host welcomed them warmly.
Notes: matron 年长已婚妇女/女主管；非贬，指‘稳重丰润’。
SynonymDistinction: stately 庄严；matronly 特指‘成熟主妇般的丰润庄重’。

Definition: 义1. （男子）衣冠楚楚的；精干的
Examples:
义1:
  • A dapper old gentleman tipped his hat.
  • He looked dapper in a waistcoat.
  • The dapper clerk bowed slightly.
Notes: small and neat 小个子但整洁利落；常带欣赏。
SynonymDistinction: smart 整洁帅；dapper 强调‘小而精致、利落有型’。

Examples:
义1:
  • His sallow skin betrayed fatigue.
  • The patient looked sallow and drawn.
  • A sallow complexion needs warm tones.
Notes: 非 tan（晒黑）；sallow 是‘不健康枯黄’。
SynonymDistinction: pallid 苍白；sallow 偏‘黄而病态’；ruddy 红润健康。

Definition: 义1. 沉着的；不为所动的
Examples:
义1:
  • She stayed imperturbable under fire.
  • His imperturbable calm reassured the crew.
  • The diplomat was imperturbable in crisis.
Notes: perturb 使不安；imperturbable ‘泰山崩于前而色不变’。
SynonymDistinction: composed 镇定；imperturbable 强调‘根本无法被扰动’。

Definition: 义1. （言谈）过分奉承的；油腻的
Examples:
义1:
  • The salesman gave an unctuous smile.
  • His unctuous praise rang false.
  • She found his unctuous manner offensive.
Notes: 贬义；原指‘油滑’，喻‘虚伪热情’。
SynonymDistinction: fulsome 过度到令人不适的；unctuous 强调‘油嘴滑舌、谄媚’。

Definition: 义1. 爱抱怨的；易怒的
Examples:
义1:
  • A querulous old man grumbled on.
  • Her querulous tone alienated friends.
  • He grew querulous in his illness.
Notes: 常形容老人/病人‘动辄怨天尤人’；名词 querulousness。
SynonymDistinction: peevish 小脾气；querulous 持续‘抱怨不休’。

Definition: 义1. 暴躁的；易生气的
Examples:
义1:
  • A choleric boss terrified the staff.
  • His choleric temper flared at trifles.
  • The choleric old man stamped his stick.
Notes: 四体液说 choler 胆汁质；与 phlegmatic 相反。
SynonymDistinction: irascible 易怒；choleric 古典‘胆汁质暴躁’。

Definition: 义1. 情绪多变的；反复无常的
Examples:
义1:
  • His volatile moods unsettled the team.
  • A volatile crowd turned ugly fast.
  • She is volatile, laughing then sulking.
Notes: 也形容市场/物质易变；volatile temperament 情绪不稳。
SynonymDistinction: mercurial 多变善变（可褒可贬）；volatile 偏‘危险地易爆发’。

Examples:
义1:
  • An intrepid explorer crossed the ice.
  • The intrepid climber scaled the cliff.
  • She is an intrepid traveller.
Notes: 褒义；intrepidity 无畏；近 brave 但更‘敢闯’。
SynonymDistinction: brave 一般勇敢；intrepid 强调‘面对未知危险仍无畏’。

Definition: 义1. 一丝不苟的；过分讲究的
Examples:
义1:
  • He is fastidious about grammar.
  • A fastidious host arranged everything just so.
  • She is fastidious to a fault about cleanliness.
Notes: 可褒（细致）可贬（挑剔）；名词 fastidiousness。
SynonymDistinction: meticulous 细致；fastidious 强调‘对细节过分讲究/挑剔’。

Definition: 义1. 无忧无虑的；轻率的
Examples:
义1:
  • She sang with blithe cheer.
  • His blithe disregard for rules cost him.
  • A blithe spirit danced through life.
Notes: blithe 可褒‘快乐无忧’也可贬‘轻率不在意’。
SynonymDistinction: carefree 无忧；blithe 多带‘不在意后果’的轻率感。

Examples:
义1:
  • The train crossed a vast plateau.
  • Sales hit a plateau last quarter.
  • The plateau rises gently to the east.
Notes: 地理‘高原’；也喻‘停滞平台期’。
SynonymDistinction: highland 高地；plateau 平坦的高原面。

Examples:
义1:
  • The glacier calves ice into the sea.
  • Glaciers carved the valley over ages.
  • The glacier is retreating fast.
Notes: calve 崩冰；retreat 退缩（气候变暖）。

Examples:
义1:
  • Sediment settled at the bottom.
  • The river carries rich sediment.
  • Layers of sediment built the plain.
Notes: sedimentary 沉积岩；deposit 堆积。

Examples:
义1:
  • The region's topography is rugged.
  • Topography shapes local climate.
  • They mapped the topography in detail.
Notes: topographic 地形的；relief 地势起伏。
SynonymDistinction: terrain 地形（可通行）；topography 是‘地形学/地貌特征’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The arid desert receives little rain.
  • Arid conditions limit farming.
  • The soil is arid and cracked.
Notes: 名词 aridity；反义 humid / fertile。
SynonymDistinction: dry 干；arid 强调‘长期缺水不宜生长’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The aurora is a natural phenomenon.
  • Climate change is a global phenomenon.
  • This social phenomenon puzzled researchers.
Notes: 复数 phenomena；phenomenal 非凡的。
SynonymDistinction: event 事件；phenomenon 可观察的‘现象/事物’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Meteorology predicts the weather.
  • He studied meteorology at university.
  • Satellite data aids meteorology.
Notes: meteorologist 气象学家；注意与 meteorite 陨石无关。

Examples:
义1:
  • Cubism fractured form into facets.
  • Picasso pioneered Cubism.
  • Cubism shows many views at once.
Notes: Picasso / Braque；multi-perspective 多视角。

Definition: 义1. 调色板；（用色）范畴
Examples:
义1:
  • The painter's palette was muted.
  • Her palette favoured blues and greys.
  • The film's palette is cold and grey.
Notes: 注意与 palate（上颚/味觉）、pallet（托盘）同音不同义。
SynonymDistinction: colour scheme 配色方案；palette 本义‘调色板’，引申‘所用色彩范围’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The composition balances dark and light.
  • He studied musical composition.
  • The photograph's composition is striking.
Notes: 绘画‘构图’、音乐‘作曲’、文学‘写作’通用。
SynonymDistinction: layout 版面排布；composition 艺术‘构图/曲式结构’。

Definition: 义1. （演员/乐团的）演出曲目；全部本领
Examples:
义1:
  • The pianist's repertoire is vast.
  • They added the piece to the repertoire.
  • She has a wide repertoire of skills.
Notes: 表演‘保留剧目/曲库’；也喻‘全部技能库’。

Definition: 义1. （团体/时代的）精神气质
Examples:
义1:
  • The ethos of the school is rigorous.
  • The film captures the ethos of the 60s.
  • Its ethos values freedom over order.
Notes: 亚里士多德修辞三诉求之一（ethos/pathos/logos）；精神特质。
SynonymDistinction: spirit 精神；ethos 指‘共同体深层的价值观与气质’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The avant-garde shocked audiences.
  • She favours avant-garde cinema.
  • The gallery shows avant-garde work.
Notes: 法语‘先遣队’；指艺术上激进前卫。
SynonymDistinction: experimental 实验性；avant-garde 强调‘走在最前、挑战成规’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The tower is the city's landmark.
  • We photographed every landmark.
  • The law was a landmark in civil rights.
Notes: 地理‘地标’；喻‘重大里程碑’。
SynonymDistinction: monument 纪念碑；landmark 可指自然地标/标志建筑。

Examples:
义1:
  • They stayed at a beach resort.
  • The ski resort opened in December.
  • A luxury resort lined the bay.
Notes: 也作动词 resort to‘诉诸’；last resort 最后手段。
SynonymDistinction: destination 目的地；resort 专指‘度假疗养地’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The hotel caters weddings.
  • The menu caters to vegetarians.
  • They catered for 200 guests.
Notes: cater to 迎合需求；caterer 餐饮承办。
SynonymDistinction: serve 服务；cater 专指‘承办饮食/迎合特定需求’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The hill offered a wide vista.
  • A vista of rooftops opened below.
  • The valley revealed a stunning vista.
Notes: long view 远景；与 view 近但更‘开阔深远’。
SynonymDistinction: view 一般视野；vista 强调‘延伸的远景/林荫道尽头的景’。

Examples:
义1:
  • A weary wayfarer rested at the inn.
  • The poem follows a lone wayfarer.
  • Wayfarers crossed the mountain pass.
Notes: 文学/古雅用词；近 traveller 但更诗意。
SynonymDistinction: traveller 旅行者；wayfarer 文雅‘行旅之人’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The local currency is the baht.
  • Exchange your currency at the bank.
  • The idea gained currency among youth.
Notes: foreign currency 外汇；也指‘流传/通用’。
SynonymDistinction: money 钱；currency 指‘流通的货币种类’。

Definition: 义1. 查理曼（742–814，法兰克国王，加洛林王朝）
Examples:
义1:
  • Charlemagne united much of Western Europe.
  • Charlemagne was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 800.
  • The Carolingian Renaissance bore his name.
Notes: 法兰克国王/神圣罗马皇帝；推广教育、加洛林文艺复兴。

Definition: 义1. 威廉·莎士比亚（1564–1616，英国剧作家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Shakespeare wrote about 39 plays.
  • Shakespeare shaped the English language itself.
  • Hamlet is Shakespeare's most famous tragedy.
Notes: ‘ Bard of Avon’；sonnets +  tragedies/comedies 奠基英语文学。

Definition: 义1. 拿破仑·波拿巴（1769–1821，法国皇帝）
Examples:
义1:
  • Napoleon rose in the Revolution's wake.
  • Napoleon was defeated at Waterloo in 1815.
  • The Napoleonic Code reshaped law.
Notes: 军事天才；法典影响大陆法系；滑铁卢战败。

Definition: 义1. 卡尔·马克思（1818–1883，哲学家/经济学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Marx co-wrote The Communist Manifesto.
  • Marx analysed capital and class struggle.
  • Marx's ideas shaped the 20th century.
Notes: 《资本论》《共产党宣言》；historical materialism 历史唯物主义。

Definition: 义1. 弗洛伦斯·南丁格尔（1820–1910，现代护理奠基人）
Examples:
义1:
  • Nightingale reformed military nursing.
  • Nightingale pioneered health statistics.
  • The Lady with the Lamp served in Crimea.
Notes: ‘提灯女神’；现代护理与卫生统计之父（母）。

Definition: 义1. 罗莎·帕克斯（1913–2005，民权运动者）
Examples:
义1:
  • Parks refused to give up her bus seat.
  • Parks sparked the Montgomery bus boycott.
  • Parks became an icon of civil rights.
Notes: 1955 蒙哥马利巴士抵制运动导火索。

Definition: 义1. 玛丽·居里（1867–1934，物理学家/化学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Curie discovered radium and polonium.
  • Curie won Nobel Prizes in two sciences.
  • Curie pioneered research on radioactivity.
Notes: 首位两获诺奖、跨物理与化学；radioactivity 放射性。

Definition: 义1. 艾伦·图灵（1912–1954，计算机科学先驱）
Examples:
义1:
  • Turing devised the Turing machine.
  • Turing broke the Enigma code in WWII.
  • Turing founded the theory of computation.
Notes: 图灵机、人工智能之父；破解 Enigma。

Definition: 义1. 司马迁（约前145–前86，中国史学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Sima Qian wrote the Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian).
  • Sima Qian endured castration yet finished his history.
  • The Shiji shaped Chinese historiography for millennia.
Notes: 《史记》纪传体通史之祖；‘史家之绝唱’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Zheng He led seven voyages to the Indian Ocean.
  • Zheng He's fleets reached Africa and Arabia.
  • Zheng He sailed decades before Columbus.
Notes: 三宝太监；宝船下西洋，早于大航海。

Definition: 义1. 秦始皇（前259–前210，中国首位皇帝）
Examples:
义1:
  • Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BCE.
  • He ordered the Great Wall and the Terracotta Army.
  • His reforms standardised writing and weights.
Notes: 统一文字度量衡；兵马俑；焚书坑儒争议。

Definition: 义1. 伊本·白图泰（1304–1369，摩洛哥旅行家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Ibn Battuta travelled across three continents.
  • His Rihla records medieval Eurasia and Africa.
  • He voyaged farther than Marco Polo.
Notes: 《游记》Rihla；伊斯兰世界最伟大旅行家。

Examples:
义1:
  • Sun Yat-sen founded the Republic of China in 1912.
  • He promoted the Three Principles of the People.
  • Sun is honoured as the ‘Father of the Nation’.
Notes: 辛亥革命；三民主义；推翻帝制。

Definition: 义1. 背包客；自助旅行者
Examples:
义1:
  • The hostel was full of backpackers.
  • Backpackers roam Southeast Asia on a budget.
  • He travelled as a backpacker for a year.
Notes: budget travel 穷游；hostel 青旅。

Examples:
义1:
  • They took a Mediterranean cruise.
  • The ship cruised past the cliffs.
  • A cruise is an easy way to see many ports.
Notes: cruise ship 游轮；也指‘悠闲巡航’。

Examples:
义1:
  • They made a pilgrimage to Mecca.
  • Fans treat the shrine as a pilgrimage.
  • The pilgrimage crossed the mountains.
Notes: pilgrim 朝圣者；也喻‘心驰神往的旅程’。

Definition: 义1. 集市；（东方）露天市场
Examples:
义1:
  • The bazaar teemed with spices and silk.
  • We haggled at the night bazaar.
  • The old bazaar smelled of incense.
Notes: 中东/南亚市场；haggle 讨价还价。

Examples:
义1:
  • The summit offered a vast panorama.
  • The window framed a panorama of the bay.
  • The city panorama lit up at dusk.
Notes: panoramic 全景的；比 view 更‘一览无余’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The emporium sold goods from afar.
  • A grand emporium anchored the square.
  • The Christmas emporium drew crowds.
Notes: 文学/古雅；近 department store。

Definition: 义1. 青年旅舍；招待所
Examples:
义1:
  • We stayed in a cheap hostel.
  • The hostel had a shared kitchen.
  • Backpackers favour hostels over hotels.
Notes: shared dorm 多人间；budget lodging。

Definition: 义1. 屈服；因…而死（succumb to）
Examples:
义1:
  • He succumbed to the altitude.
  • Many succumbed to the desert heat.
  • She succumbed to temptation and bought it.
Notes: 正式；succumb to 死于/屈从于。

Examples:
义1:
  • His sojourn in Paris lasted a year.
  • A brief sojourn by the lake refreshed her.
  • The poet's sojourn abroad shaped his work.
Notes: 文学‘短暂停留’；比 stay 雅致。

Examples:
义1:
  • A caravan crossed the dunes at dawn.
  • They rented a caravan for the trip.
  • The caravan of camels stretched for miles.
Notes: 商队/驼队；英式也指‘房车’（美 RV）。

Examples:
义1:
  • The nomads followed the herds.
  • Digital nomads work from anywhere.
  • Once a nomad, he settled at last.
Notes: nomadic 游牧的；digital nomad 数字游民。

Examples:
义1:
  • We strolled the cobbled lane.
  • The cobbled square buzzed with cafés.
  • Cobbled streets charm old towns.
Notes: cobble 鹅卵石；cobblestone 同义。

Examples:
义1:
  • The village was utterly enchanting.
  • An enchanting garden lay behind the wall.
  • The music was soft and enchanting.
Notes: enchant 使迷醉；比 charming 更‘魔法般’。

Examples:
义1:
  • A quaint cottage nestled in the hill.
  • The town has quaint little shops.
  • They loved the quaint harbour.
Notes: 褒义‘小巧古雅’；有时略带‘过时可爱’。

Definition: 义1. 旅行癖；漫游渴望
Examples:
义1:
  • Wanderlust drove him abroad.
  • She felt a sudden wanderlust.
  • The book fed his wanderlust.
Notes: 德语借词；lust 渴望 + wander 漫游。

Examples:
义1:
  • An expedition mapped the glacier.
  • They joined an Arctic expedition.
  • The expedition returned after months.
Notes: explore 探险；military expedition 远征军。

Examples:
义1:
  • The museum kept a relic of the saint.
  • Ruins are relics of a lost city.
  • The relic drew pilgrims for centuries.
Notes: relic 圣物/遗骸；也指‘陈旧残余’。

Examples:
义1:
  • We took a jaunt to the coast.
  • A Sunday jaunt lifted his mood.
  • The jaunt lasted but an afternoon.
Notes: 轻松愉快的短途；近 outing。

Examples:
义1:
  • They stayed in a mountain lodge.
  • We lodged with local villagers.
  • The hunting lodge sat by the lake.
Notes: lodge 小木屋/旅舍；也指‘正式提出’（lodge a complaint）。

Examples:
义1:
  • The lake was perfectly serene.
  • A serene sunset calmed the crowd.
  • She kept a serene expression.
Notes: serenity 宁静；比 calm 更‘平和优美’。

Examples:
义1:
  • We walked home in the twilight.
  • The town glowed at twilight.
  • Fireflies appeared at twilight.
Notes: dawn/dusk；也喻‘衰落期’（the twilight of his career）。

Definition: 义1. 热带草原（稀树草原）
Examples:
义1:
  • Lions roam the African savanna.
  • The savanna burns dry each winter.
  • Acacia dot the savanna.
Notes: 热带草原生态；与 grassland 不同更热。

Examples:
义1:
  • The fjord cut deep into the coast.
  • A cruise entered the narrow fjord.
  • Norway is famed for its fjords.
Notes: 冰川侵蚀的狭长海湾；挪威特色地貌。

Examples:
义1:
  • The Nile delta is fertile.
  • The river fanned into a delta.
  • Sediment built the delta over centuries.
Notes: 河流入海泥沙堆积；与 estuary 河口不同。

Examples:
义1:
  • An oasis broke the desert monotony.
  • The garden was an oasis of calm.
  • Camels rested at the oasis.
Notes: 沙漠中的水源地；喻‘慰藉之所’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The city lies in a river basin.
  • The Amazon basin is vast.
  • Sediment filled the geological basin.
Notes: river basin 流域；geological basin 盆地。

Examples:
义1:
  • We climbed the rocky ridge.
  • Snow capped the ridge.
  • The ridge divides two valleys.
Notes: mountain ridge 山脊；与 peak 峰不同。

Examples:
义1:
  • The river wound through the valley.
  • Mist hung in the valley.
  • They farmed the fertile valley floor.
Notes: 与 ridge 相对；river valley 河谷。

Examples:
义1:
  • Ships passed through the strait.
  • The strait links two seas.
  • The Strait of Gibraltar guards the Mediterranean.
Notes: 窄水道；与 channel 近义。

Examples:
义1:
  • The river carved a deep gorge.
  • A bridge spanned the gorge.
  • The gorge echoed with the falls.
Notes: 深窄峡谷；canyon 更大更宽。

Examples:
义1:
  • Cows grazed the flowering meadow.
  • The meadow glowed with buttercups.
  • They picnicked in the meadow.
Notes: 野生花草草地；与 lawn 草坪不同。

Examples:
义1:
  • Reeds swayed in the marsh.
  • The marsh teemed with birds.
  • They drained the marsh for farmland.
Notes: marshland；与 swamp 近（swamp 树木多）。

Examples:
义1:
  • The volcano erupted at dawn.
  • Lava flowed down the volcano.
  • The volcano has been dormant for years.
Notes: erupt 喷发；dormant 休眠；magma 岩浆。

Examples:
义1:
  • The tsunami swept the coast.
  • A quake triggered the tsunami.
  • Warning systems spotted the tsunami.
Notes: 日语借词；地震引发的海浪。

Examples:
义1:
  • The equator splits the globe.
  • The climate is hot near the equator.
  • They crossed the equator at sea.
Notes: equatorial 赤道的；0°纬线。

Examples:
义1:
  • The city lies at high latitude.
  • Latitude affects the climate.
  • The rule gives judges some latitude.
Notes: 地理‘纬度’；喻‘自由裁量余地’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The current carried the raft seaward.
  • The Gulf Stream is a warm current.
  • Ocean currents shape the climate.
Notes: ocean current 洋流；也指‘时下的’（current affairs）。

Examples:
义1:
  • The slope was bare of vegetation.
  • Dense vegetation hid the ruins.
  • Altitude limits the vegetation.
Notes: 总称‘植物覆盖’；非单株 plant。

Definition: 义1. 生物多样性热点区
Examples:
义1:
  • Madagascar is a biodiversity hotspot.
  • The hotspot hosts many endemics.
  • Conservation targets biodiversity hotspots.
Notes: endemic 特有种；热点区物种极丰富但受威胁。

Examples:
义1:
  • Permafrost underlies the tundra.
  • Thawing permafrost releases methane.
  • Buildings sink as permafrost melts.
Notes: 永久冻结土层；北极/高山。

Examples:
义1:
  • The desert is a harsh biome.
  • Each biome has distinct life.
  • Climate defines the biome.
Notes: 大尺度生态区（雨林/苔原等）；ecosystem 更小。

Examples:
义1:
  • Sci-fi is a popular genre.
  • The novel crosses several genres.
  • Each genre has its conventions.
Notes: 文学/电影/音乐‘体裁’； conventions 惯例。

Examples:
义1:
  • The design has a clean aesthetic.
  • She has a minimalist aesthetic.
  • Aesthetic value matters here.
Notes: aesthetics 美学；也指‘外观品味’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The sculpture depicted a horse.
  • She studied sculpture at art school.
  • Marble sculpture lined the hall.
Notes: sculpt 雕塑（动词）；sculptor 雕塑家。

Examples:
义1:
  • A mural covered the wall.
  • The mural celebrated the town's history.
  • Artists painted a street mural.
Notes: mural 墙上的画；与 fresco 湿壁画相关。

Examples:
义1:
  • The lines show linear perspective.
  • The artist fixed the perspective.
  • From this perspective the figure recedes.
Notes: 绘画‘透视法’；也指‘观点’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The red contrasts with the green.
  • High contrast sharpens the image.
  • The essay contrasts two views.
Notes: contrast 对比；与 compare 比较不同。

Examples:
义1:
  • The orchestra tuned before the show.
  • She joined the youth orchestra.
  • The orchestra played Beethoven.
Notes: conductor 指挥；symphony orchestra 交响乐团。

Examples:
义1:
  • He played a violin solo.
  • The solo drew loud applause.
  • She sang a solo in the choir.
Notes: soloist 独奏者；与 ensemble 合奏相对。

Examples:
义1:
  • The choir sang at the service.
  • The school choir toured Europe.
  • The choir's harmony was pure.
Notes: chorus 合唱（也可指歌曲中的副歌）；choir 团体。

Examples:
义1:
  • The lyrics moved the crowd.
  • He wrote the music and she the lyrics.
  • The lyrics touch on loss.
Notes: lyric 也可作形容词‘抒情的’；注意复数。

Examples:
义1:
  • The rhythm drove the dancers.
  • He kept a steady rhythm.
  • The poem has a gentle rhythm.
Notes: beat 节拍；rhythm 整体节奏律动。

Examples:
义1:
  • Jazz is largely improvisational.
  • His style is bold and improvisational.
  • The scene felt improvisational.
Notes: 来 improvisation；强调‘临场发挥’。

Examples:
义1:
  • He is a piano virtuoso.
  • The virtuoso dazzled the hall.
  • Few reach virtuoso level.
Notes: 形容技艺极高者；也作形容词。

Examples:
义1:
  • She sang an octave higher.
  • The tune jumps an octave.
  • The scale spans two octaves.
Notes: 音乐音程；八度音。

Examples:
义1:
  • The hall has rich resonance.
  • His words had emotional resonance.
  • The string's resonance lingered.
Notes: resonate 共鸣；喻‘引起共鸣’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The timbre of a cello is warm.
  • Each voice has its own timbre.
  • Synthesizers mimic timbre.
Notes: 音‘色彩/质地’；法语借词，也写 timbre。

Examples:
义1:
  • The second movement is slow.
  • The symphony has four movements.
  • The art movement favoured colour.
Notes: 音乐‘乐章’；也指‘艺术/社会运动’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The hall's acoustics are superb.
  • Poor acoustics marred the concert.
  • Acoustics studies how sound behaves.
Notes: 单数‘音响效果’，复数‘声学’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The antagonist thwarts the hero.
  • The antagonist is not purely evil.
  • A worthy antagonist sharpens the plot.
Notes: 与 protagonist 相对；未必是‘坏人’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The narrator is unreliable.
  • A first-person narrator tells the tale.
  • The narrator comments on the action.
Notes: narrative 叙事；unreliable narrator 不可靠叙述者（高频考点）。

Examples:
义1:
  • A romance forms the subplot.
  • The subplot mirrors the main plot.
  • The subplot resolves by the end.
Notes: main plot 主情节；subplot 支线。

Examples:
义1:
  • ‘The Great’ is an epithet.
  • Homer uses fixed epithets.
  • He earned the epithet ‘the Wise’.
Notes: 描述性形容词/称号；有时指‘贬称’。

Definition: 义1. 从中间入手（开篇即高潮）
Examples:
义1:
  • The epic opens in medias res.
  • The film begins in medias res.
  • In medias res hooks the reader fast.
Notes: 拉丁‘in the middle of things’；叙事技巧。

Examples:
义1:
  • Lycidas is a pastoral elegy.
  • The pastoral elegy mourns a shepherd.
  • Milton wrote a famous pastoral elegy.
Notes: 结合田园+哀悼；如 Milton 的 Lycidas。

Examples:
义1:
  • The ballad told of a lost love.
  • A folk ballad circled the village.
  • He set the ballad to music.
Notes: 叙事性歌谣；ballad stanza 民谣诗节。

Examples:
义1:
  • Keats wrote an ode to a nightingale.
  • The ode praises autumn.
  • An ode addresses its subject directly.
Notes: lyric poem 抒情诗的一种；直接赞颂。

Examples:
义1:
  • The novel opens with an epigraph.
  • The epigraph sets the tone.
  • He chose a line from Dante as epigraph.
Notes: 置于作品前的引语；与 epilogue 尾声不同。

Examples:
义1:
  • The cartoon was a caricature of the mayor.
  • He drew a cruel caricature.
  • The speech was a caricature of reason.
Notes: 夸张讽刺画/文；也作动词。

Definition: 义1. 有症状的；作为征兆的
Examples:
义1:
  • He is symptomatic and must isolate.
  • The rash is symptomatic of allergy.
  • Low turnout is symptomatic of apathy.
Notes: 反义 asymptomatic 无症状；也喻‘是…征兆’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The marker is prognostic of outcome.
  • Prognostic factors guide treatment.
  • Age is a prognostic variable.
Notes: 来自 prognosis；predictive 预测性。

Examples:
义1:
  • The cancer is in remission.
  • She has been in remission for years.

Examples:
义1:
  • The elephant's tusk gleamed.
  • Poachers took the tusk.
  • The walrus raised a tusk.
Notes: 象牙/海象牙；ivory 象牙制品。

Examples:
义1:
  • Poultry farms dot the county.
  • The market sold live poultry.
  • Poultry provides meat and eggs.
Notes: chicken/duck/turkey 总称；也指禽肉。

Examples:
义1:
  • The drought killed the livestock.
  • Livestock grazed the range.
  • They insured the livestock.
Notes: 牛/羊/猪等农畜总称。

Examples:
义1:
  • Cattle graze the meadow.
  • The sheep grazed all day.
  • He grazed his knee on the rock.
Notes: 动物吃草；也指‘轻擦（伤）’。

Definition: 义1. 荷马（约前8C，希腊史诗诗人）
Examples:
义1:
  • Homer wrote the Iliad and Odyssey.
  • Homer shaped Western epic.
  • Scholars debate if Homer was one man.
Notes: 《伊利亚特》《奥德赛》；blind poet 传说。

Definition: 义1. 奥古斯都（前63–14，罗马首位皇帝）
Examples:
义1:
  • Augustus founded the Empire.
  • Augustus ended the civil wars.
  • The Pax Romana began under Augustus.
Notes: 屋大维；Roman Empire 开端；Pax Romana 罗马和平。

Definition: 义1. 路易·巴斯德（1822–1895，微生物学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Pasteur proved germs cause disease.
  • Pasteur invented pasteurisation.
  • He developed vaccines against rabies.
Notes: 巴氏消毒；germ theory 病菌说；疫苗。

Definition: 义1. 托马斯·爱迪生（1847–1931，发明家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Edison patented the light bulb.
  • Edison built the first lab.
  • He held over a thousand patents.
Notes: 电灯/留声机；inventor 发明家。

Definition: 义1. 阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦（1879–1955，物理学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Einstein proposed relativity.
  • Einstein's E=mc² reshaped physics.
  • He fled Nazi Germany in 1933.
Notes: 相对论；光电效应诺奖；20C 科学象征。

Examples:
义1:
  • Mao led the Communist revolution in 1949.
  • Mao wrote poetry and essays.
  • His thought shaped modern China.
Notes: 新中国成立；兼具政治家与诗人身份。

Definition: 义1. 邓小平（1904–1997，中国改革设计师）
Examples:
义1:
  • Deng launched Reform and Opening-up.
  • Deng promoted ‘Socialism with Chinese characteristics’.
  • His pragmatism transformed the economy.
Notes: 改革开放；‘黑猫白猫’论；现代化推手。

Definition: 义1. 乔治·华盛顿（1732–1799，美国首任总统）
Examples:
义1:
  • Washington led the Revolution.
  • Washington was the first U.S. president.
  • He refused a crown, setting a precedent.
Notes: ‘国父’；两任后隐退；precedent 先例。

Definition: 义1. 富兰克林·罗斯福（1882–1945，美国总统）
Examples:
义1:
  • FDR led the U.S. through the Depression and WWII.
  • He launched the New Deal.
  • He was elected four times.
Notes: 新政 New Deal；唯一四任总统；二战领袖。

Definition: 义1. 玛格丽特·撒切尔（1925–2013，英国首相）
Examples:
义1:
  • Thatcher was Britain's first woman PM.
  • Thatcher promoted free-market reform.
  • She was called the ‘Iron Lady’.
Notes: 铁娘子；保守党；新自由主义。

Definition: 义1. 伊丽莎白一世（1533–1603，英格兰女王）
Examples:
义1:
  • Elizabeth I reigned in a golden age.
  • She defeated the Spanish Armada.
  • The Elizabethan era blossomed in arts.
Notes: 都铎；黄金时代；Shakespeare 同期。

Examples:
义1:
  • Peter modernised Russia by force.
  • He built the city of St Petersburg.
  • Peter opened a window to the West.
Notes: 西化改革；俄罗斯帝国。

Definition: 义1. 叶卡捷琳娜大帝（1729–1796，俄国女皇）
Examples:
义1:
  • Catherine expanded the empire.
  • She patronised the arts and law.
  • Her reign was an age of enlightenment.
Notes: 俄国黄金时代；启蒙专制。

Examples:
义1:
  • Bismarck united Germany by realpolitik.
  • He engineered wars to unify the states.
  • Bismarck built the welfare state.
Notes: 铁血宰相；realpolitik 现实政治；德意志统一。

Definition: 义1. 莫罕达斯·甘地（即 Mahatma Gandhi）
Examples:
义1:
  • Gandhi led non-violent resistance.
  • His Salt March challenged British rule.
  • Gandhi inspired civil-rights movements.
Notes: satyagraha 非暴力；印度独立。

Definition: 义1. 忽必烈（1215–1294，元朝开国皇帝）
Examples:
义1:
  • Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty.
  • He completed the conquest of China.
  • Marco Polo visited his court.
Notes: 元世祖；蒙古帝国中原政权；大都。

Definition: 义1. 图坦卡蒙（前1341–前1323，埃及法老）
Examples:
义1:
  • Tutankhamun's tomb was found intact in 1922.
  • The boy king ruled briefly.
  • His gold mask is world-famous.
Notes: 最完整法老墓；1922 Carter 发现。

Examples:
义1:
  • The report delineates three policy options.
  • We must delineate the scope before analysis.
  • The map delineates the fault lines.
Notes: 近 outline，但更强调‘勾画边界/范围’。
SynonymDistinction: delineate 偏‘划出清晰边界’；outline 偏‘列要点’。

Definition: 义1. 开创性的；影响深远的
Examples:
义1:
  • His seminal paper reshaped the field.
  • That book is a seminal work on cognition.
  • The seminal study spawned a new discipline.
Notes: 形容著作/研究‘奠基性’，褒义强。
SynonymDistinction: seminal 强调‘开创先河’；influential 仅指‘有影响’。

Definition: 义1. （标准、规定）严格的；苛刻的
Examples:
义1:
  • Stringent rules govern clinical trials.
  • The bank faces stringent capital requirements.
  • We need more stringent emission standards.
Notes: 常接 rules/controls/standards/tests。
SynonymDistinction: stringent 多用于规章标准；strict 通用。

Definition: 义1. （论点）站得住脚的；可防守的
Examples:
义1:
  • That position is no longer tenable.
  • Is the hypothesis tenable given the data?
  • He held a barely tenable view.
Notes: 常用于否定：no longer tenable。

Definition: 义1. 虚假的；站不住脚的
Examples:
义1:
  • The study’s claims are spurious.
  • He offered a spurious justification.
  • Spurious correlations mislead readers.
Notes: spurious correlation 是常见搭配（伪相关）。
SynonymDistinction: spurious 强调‘看似有理实则假’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The contract stipulates a 30-day notice.
  • The grant stipulates how funds are used.
  • The law stipulates minimum standards.
Notes: 正式‘明文规定’，后接 that 或名词。
SynonymDistinction: stipulate 偏法律/正式规定；specify 中性‘具体说明’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Lack of data precludes a conclusion.
  • His age does not preclude the role.
  • The rule precludes appeals.
Notes: preclude sb from doing / preclude sth。
SynonymDistinction: preclude 正式‘使不可能’；prevent 通用。

Examples:
义1:
  • He has a propensity for risk.
  • Firms show a propensity to overhire.
  • There is a propensity toward errors.
Notes: propensity for / to / toward。
SynonymDistinction: propensity 偏‘固有倾向’；tendency 更中性通用。

Examples:
义1:
  • Ask pertinent questions only.
  • The evidence is pertinent to the case.
  • She made a pertinent observation.
Notes: pertinent to。
SynonymDistinction: pertinent 正式‘切题’；relevant 通用。

Definition: 义1. 明确的；毫不含糊的
Examples:
义1:
  • The data give unequivocal support.
  • He issued an unequivocal denial.
  • The verdict was unequivocal.
Notes: 强调‘无歧义’，程度强于 clear。

Examples:
义1:
  • We must reconcile the two findings.
  • Theory and data are hard to reconcile.
  • He reconciled the conflicting accounts.
Notes: reconcile A with B。

Definition: 义1. 脆弱的；微弱的；牵强的
Examples:
义1:
  • The link is tenuous at best.
  • They have a tenuous hold on power.
  • His argument rests on a tenuous analogy.
Notes: tenuous link/connection 常见。
SynonymDistinction: tenuous 指‘薄弱、易断’（物理/逻辑皆可）。

Definition: 义1. 相称的；成比例的
Examples:
义1:
  • Pay should be commensurate with effort.
  • A penalty commensurate with the crime.
  • Funding is not commensurate with need.
Notes: commensurate with。

Definition: 义1. 使模糊；故意混淆
Examples:
义1:
  • Jargon obfuscates the issue.
  • He obfuscated his role in the affair.
  • The report obfuscates the real costs.
Notes: 贬义‘把事情搞糊涂’，尤指故意。
SynonymDistinction: obfuscate 比 confuse 更正式且含‘故意遮掩’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Good writers eschew cliché.
  • The firm eschews debt.
  • She eschews publicity.
Notes: 正式‘刻意回避’，及物。
SynonymDistinction: eschew 正式‘主动戒绝’；avoid 通用。

Examples:
义1:
  • He enumerated three objections.
  • The risks were enumerated clearly.
  • Let me enumerate the steps.
Notes: 比 list 正式，强调‘逐一列出’。
SynonymDistinction: enumerate 正式‘逐条枚举’。

Examples:
义1:
  • There is a discrepancy in the accounts.
  • We found a discrepancy between the two figures.
  • The discrepancy remains unexplained.
Notes: discrepancy between A and B。

Examples:
义1:
  • We reached a provisional agreement.
  • The figures are provisional.
  • A provisional government was formed.
Notes: provisional 与 tentative 近义，但更偏‘暂时生效’。

Definition: 义1. 赞助；主持（under the auspices of）
Examples:
义1:
  • The summit met under UN auspices.
  • Research was done under academic auspices.
  • The project ran under private auspices.
Notes: 几乎只用 under the auspices of 短语。

Examples:
义1:
  • The court nullified the law.
  • The goal was nullified by offside.
  • The gain was nullified by costs.
Notes: 法律/正式‘作废’。
SynonymDistinction: nullify 正式‘宣告无效’；cancel 通用。

Examples:
义1:
  • The letter purports to be official.
  • The study purports to show a link.
  • What does the clause purport to mean?
Notes: 常带‘声称（未必属实）’的意味。
SynonymDistinction: purport 暗示‘表面宣称’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Documents pertaining to the case.
  • Matters pertaining to safety.
  • Files pertaining to tax.
Notes: 正式书面语，= relating to。

Examples:
义1:
  • She made a cogent argument.
  • The case is cogent and clear.
  • We need more cogent evidence.
Notes: cogent reason/argument/evidence。
SynonymDistinction: cogent 专指‘逻辑上有力’。

Definition: 义1. 提喻（以部分代全体）
Examples:
义1:
  • ‘All hands on deck’ is synecdoche.
  • ‘The crown’ for the monarchy is synecdoche.
  • Synecdoche links part to whole.
Notes: 部分代整体，与 metonymy（相关代）易混。
SynonymDistinction: synecdoche 必为‘部分—整体’；metonymy 是‘相关’代（如 White House=政府）。

Definition: 义1. 移情谬误（将人性赋予自然）
Examples:
义1:
  • The angry storm is pathetic fallacy.
  • Romantics used pathetic fallacy often.
  • ‘Nature wept’ shows pathetic fallacy.
Notes: 把人的情感投射到无生命自然。

Definition: 义1. 框架叙事（故事套故事）
Examples:
义1:
  • The Canterbury Tales uses a frame narrative.
  • A frame narrative encloses tales.
  • The film is a frame narrative.
Notes: 嵌套结构，如《西游记》取经框架内的单元故事。

Definition: 义1. 悲剧性缺陷（亚里士多德语）
Examples:
义1:
  • Oedipus’ pride is his hamartia.
  • Hamartia drives the tragic fall.
  • The hero’s hamartia is hubris.
Notes: 悲剧主人公的性格弱点，导致陨落。

Definition: 义1. 主导动机（反复出现的主题）
Examples:
义1:
  • A leitmotif recurs in the novel.
  • Wagner coined the leitmotif.
  • The colour red is a leitmotif.
Notes: 音乐/文学中反复出现的意象或旋律。

Definition: 义1. 发现／顿悟（悲剧转折点）
Examples:
义1:
  • The anagnorisis reveals the truth.
  • Oedipus’ anagnorisis is devastating.
  • Recognition drives the plot.
Notes: 主人公‘发现真相’的时刻，常与 peripeteia（逆转）成对。

Examples:
义1:
  • The peripeteia flips the fortune.
  • A sudden peripeteia shocks the reader.
  • Peripeteia follows anagnorisis.
Notes: 命运/情节的急剧反转。

Definition: 义1. 套盒结构（画中画／故事中故事）
Examples:
义1:
  • The play is a mise en abyme.
  • A story within a story is mise en abyme.
  • The film frames a film.
Notes: 法文，指‘无限嵌套’的视觉/叙事结构。

Definition: 义1. 艺格敷词（以文字描摹艺术品）
Examples:
义1:
  • The poem is an ekphrasis of a painting.
  • Ekphrasis bridges word and image.
  • He wrote ekphrasis of the statue.
Notes: 用文学描摹视觉艺术的传统。

Examples:
义1:
  • Woolf pioneered stream of consciousness.
  • The passage is pure stream of consciousness.
  • Joyce used stream of consciousness.
Notes: 内心独白式写法，代表作家 Woolf/Joyce。

Examples:
义1:
  • The narrator is unreliable by design.
  • An unreliable narrator skews the truth.
  • We doubt the unreliable narrator.
Notes: 叙述者偏见/说谎，读者须自行判断。

Examples:
义1:
  • Marquez defined magical realism.
  • Magical realism blends myth and fact.
  • The novel is magical realism.
Notes: 现实底色 + 奇幻元素，拉美文学代表。

Examples:
义1:
  • The extradition was denied.
  • They sought his extradition.
  • Extradition requires a treaty.
Notes: extradite 动词。

Examples:
义1:
  • The grand jury issued an indictment.
  • The report is an indictment of policy.
  • He faces an indictment.
Notes: indict 动词；也喻‘谴责’。
SynonymDistinction: indictment 正式刑事‘起诉’；accusation 通用‘指责’。

Examples:
义1:
  • She received a subpoena.
  • The court subpoenaed the witness.
  • He ignored the subpoena.
Notes: 法律强制出庭/取证。

Definition: 义1. 侵权（民事不法行为）
Examples:
义1:
  • Negligence is a common tort.
  • He sued in tort.
  • Tort law differs from contract.
Notes: 民事侵权，非刑事；如诽谤、过失。

Examples:
义1:
  • They sought redress in court.
  • The law provides redress.
  • We must redress the harm.
Notes: redress a grievance/wrong。

Examples:
义1:
  • They acted with impunity.
  • Impunity breeds abuse.
  • No one should enjoy impunity.
Notes: with impunity 短语。

Examples:
义1:
  • The dispute went to arbitration.
  • Arbitration avoided a lawsuit.
  • They agreed to binding arbitration.
Notes: 第三方裁决，区别于 litigation（诉讼）。
SynonymDistinction: arbitration 裁决有约束力；mediation 仅调解。

Examples:
义1:
  • Ratification needs parliament.
  • The treaty awaits ratification.
  • Ratification was swift.
Notes: ratify 动词。

Examples:
义1:
  • The system favours pluralism.
  • Cultural pluralism enriches society.
  • Pluralism checks single power.
Notes: 政治/社会‘多元共存’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Devolution gave regions power.
  • Scottish devolution changed the UK.
  • Devolution is contested.
Notes: 中央向地方放权。

Examples:
义1:
  • The impeachment failed in the senate.
  • Impeachment is a political process.
  • They launched impeachment.
Notes: impeach 动词。

Examples:
义1:
  • Embassies have extraterritorial status.
  • The base is extraterritorial.
  • Extraterritorial claims spark rows.
Notes: 法律‘超越本国领土管辖’。

Definition: 义1. 将（法律）成文化；编纂
Examples:
义1:
  • They codified customary law.
  • The rules were codified in 1990.
  • Codify the principles.
Notes: 把习惯/原则写成法典。

Examples:
义1:
  • The court issued a writ.
  • A writ of habeas corpus was filed.
  • Serve the writ.
Notes: writ of habeas corpus 人身保护令。

Examples:
义1:
  • They amended the constitution.
  • Congress amended the act.
  • The clause was amended.
Notes: amendment 修正案（如宪法修正案）。
SynonymDistinction: amend 正式‘修订（法律）’；revise 通用。

Examples:
义1:
  • The congress is bicameral.
  • A bicameral system divides power.
  • Bicameral legislatures are common.
Notes: 如美国参众两院。

Examples:
义1:
  • A pathogen entered the wound.
  • Handwashing removes pathogens.
  • The pathogen spread fast.
Notes: bacteria/virus/fungus 等致病体统称。
SynonymDistinction: pathogen 医学‘病原体’；germ 口语‘细菌’。

Examples:
义1:
  • She convalesced at home.
  • He is convalescing after surgery.
  • Convalesce by the sea.
Notes: convalescence 康复期。
SynonymDistinction: convalesce 正式‘病后静养’。

Definition: 义1. 反对的；厌恶的（averse to）
Examples:
义1:
  • He is averse to risk.
  • Patients were averse to the drug.
  • She is risk-averse.
Notes: averse to；反义 inclined。注意与 adverse（不利的）区分。
SynonymDistinction: averse ‘人反感’；adverse ‘事不利’（adverse effect）。

Definition: 义1. 特发性的（原因不明）
Examples:
义1:
  • The case is idiopathic.
  • Idiopathic hypertension has no clear cause.
  • An idiopathic fever puzzled doctors.
Notes: 医学‘查无明确病因’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Diabetes is a common comorbidity.
  • Comorbidity complicates treatment.
  • Count the comorbidities.
Notes: 同时患两种以上疾病。

Examples:
义1:
  • A nosocomial infection spread.
  • Nosocomial cases are preventable.
  • The outbreak was nosocomial.
Notes: 医院内感染（如 MRSA）。

Definition: 义1. 预防（性）的；避孕药
Examples:
义1:
  • Prophylactic antibiotics were given.
  • Use prophylactic measures.
  • A prophylactic prevents disease.
Notes: prophylaxis 预防医学。

Examples:
义1:
  • Paralysis was a sequela.
  • The sequela lingered for years.
  • Long-term sequelae worry doctors.
Notes: 复数 sequelae。
SynonymDistinction: sequela 医学‘后遗症’；aftermath 通用‘后果’。

Examples:
义1:
  • The etiology remained unknown.
  • Study the etiology of disease.
  • Etiology informs prevention.
Notes: = aetiology（英式）。

Definition: 义1. 医源性的（因治疗引起）
Examples:
义1:
  • An iatrogenic error occurred.
  • Iatrogenic harm is preventable.
  • The infection was iatrogenic.
Notes: 由医疗行为本身导致。

Examples:
义1:
  • A prodrome preceded the rash.
  • Fatigue was the prodrome.
  • Note the prodrome early.
Notes: 发病前的预警症状。

Definition: 义1. 开胃的；辛辣鲜爽的
Examples:
义1:
  • A piquant sauce lifts the meal.
  • The salsa is piquant.
  • Piquant flavours cut the fat.
Notes: 刺激味蕾、不腻。
SynonymDistinction: piquant 偏‘鲜爽刺激’；tangy 偏‘酸爽’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Duck confit is a French classic.
  • Confit preserves the meat.
  • Try the garlic confit.
Notes: 慢火油浸保存法。

Examples:
义1:
  • A wine reduction sauces the steak.
  • Make a reduction of stock.
  • The reduction was glossy.
Notes: 烹调‘收汁’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Julienne the carrots.
  • A julienne of vegetables.
  • Julienne cut aids cooking.
Notes: 细丝切法。
SynonymDistinction: julienne 法式‘细丝’；shred 通用‘切丝’。

Definition: 义1. （法餐）香料底（丁状蔬肉）
Examples:
义1:
  • A mirepoix starts the stew.
  • Sweat the mirepoix first.
  • Mirepoix builds the base.
Notes: 洋葱胡萝卜西芹切丁炒香作底。

Examples:
义1:
  • Cook the pasta al dente.
  • Al dente means firm to the bite.
  • He prefers al dente rice.
Notes: 意大利语‘有嚼劲’。

Examples:
义1:
  • Emulsify oil and vinegar.
  • Mustard helps emulsify.
  • The sauce emulsified smoothly.
Notes: 使油水混合，如蛋黄酱。

Examples:
义1:
  • A degustation menu of seven courses.
  • Degustation showcases the chef.
  • They booked the degustation.
Notes: tasting menu 品鉴菜单。

Examples:
义1:
  • A brunoise of pepper garnishes.
  • Dice to a fine brunoise.
  • Brunoise refines texture.
Notes: 比 julienne 更细的丁。

Examples:
义1:
  • A brown fond flavours the pan.
  • Deglaze the fond with wine.
  • The fond is the base.
Notes: 煎烤后锅底的焦化物，提味。

Examples:
义1:
  • A velouté of chicken.

  • Avoid the main thoroughfare.
Notes: 主要通行道路。

Examples:
义1:
  • Take the roundabout.
  • The roundabout eased the junction.
  • Exit at the second roundabout.
Notes: 环形交叉口；美式常称 traffic circle。

Examples:
义1:
  • A busy junction.
  • The junction connects two lines.
  • Wait at the junction.
Notes: 汇合点。

Examples:
义1:
  • Clear signage helps tourists.
  • The signage is bilingual.
  • Improve the signage.
Notes: 指示牌总称。

Examples:
义1:
  • Ask the concierge.
  • The concierge booked tickets.
  • A helpful concierge.
Notes: 酒店前台服务者。

Examples:
义1:
  • The hotel amenities.
  • Parks are a public amenity.
  • List the amenities.
Notes: 便利/舒适设施。

Examples:
义1:
  • Walk the rampart.
  • The rampart rings the town.
  • The rampart still stands.
Notes: 城墙/防御土垒。

Definition: 义1. 尼布甲尼撒二世（新巴比伦王）
Examples:
义1:
  • Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem.
  • Nebuchadnezzar built the Hanging Gardens (traditionally).
  • Nebuchadnezzar exiled the Jews.
Notes: 公元前 6 世纪巴比伦王，建空中花园（传说）。

Definition: 义1. 居鲁士大帝（波斯阿契美尼德开国君）
Examples:
义1:
  • Cyrus founded the Persian Empire.
  • Cyrus freed the exiled Jews.
  • Cyrus is remembered for tolerance.
Notes: 公元前 6 世纪，宽容著称。

Definition: 义1. 大流士一世（波斯王）
Examples:
义1:
  • Darius reorganized the empire.
  • Darius fought the Greeks at Marathon.
  • Darius built the royal road.
Notes: 公元前期波斯王，希波战争一方。

Definition: 义1. 征服者威廉（诺曼底公爵/英王）
Examples:
义1:
  • William conquered England in 1066.
  • William won at Hastings.
  • William commissioned the Domesday Book.
Notes: 诺曼征服，改变英国史。

Definition: 义1. 萨拉丁（阿尤布王朝苏丹）
Examples:
义1:
  • Saladin took Jerusalem.
  • Saladin fought the Crusaders.
  • Saladin was famed for chivalry.
Notes: 12 世纪穆斯林领袖，第三次十字军对手。

Examples:
义1:
  • Kublai Khan founded the Yuan dynasty.
  • Kublai Khan received Marco Polo.
  • Kublai Khan ruled China.
Notes: 蒙古帝国大汗，建元灭宋。

Definition: 义1. 马可·波罗（威尼斯旅行家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Marco Polo reached China.
  • Marco Polo served Kublai Khan.
  • Marco Polo's book awed Europe.
Notes: 13 世纪旅行者，沟通东西。

Definition: 义1. 但丁（意大利诗人）
Examples:
义1:
  • Dante wrote the Divine Comedy.
  • Dante shaped the Italian tongue.
  • Dante's Inferno is famed.
Notes: 《神曲》作者，文艺复兴前驱。

Definition: 义1. 列奥纳多·达·芬奇（文艺复兴全才）
Examples:
义1:
  • Leonardo painted the Mona Lisa.
  • Leonardo sketched flying machines.
  • Leonardo epitomized the Renaissance.
Notes: 画家/工程师/科学家。

Definition: 义1. 米开朗基罗（文艺复兴艺术巨匠）
Examples:
义1:
  • Michelangelo carved David.
  • Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel.
  • Michelangelo was a rival of Raphael.
Notes: 雕塑/绘画/建筑大师。

Definition: 义1. 伽利略（天文学家/物理学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Galileo championed the telescope.
  • Galileo was tried by the Church.
  • Galileo showed Jupiter's moons.
Notes: 近代科学奠基者之一。

Definition: 义1. 哥白尼（天文学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Copernicus proposed heliocentrism.
  • Copernicus overturned the old cosmos.
  • Copernicus influenced Galileo.
Notes: 日心说提出者。

Definition: 义1. 开普勒（天文学家）
Examples:
义1:
  • Kepler found the laws of planetary motion.
  • Kepler built on Tycho's data.
  • Kepler refined Copernicus.
Notes: 行星运动三定律。

Definition: 义1. 古腾堡（印刷术革新者）
Examples:
义1:
  • Gutenberg invented movable type in Europe.
  • Gutenberg's press spread books.
  • Gutenberg changed literacy.
Notes: 活字印刷推动知识传播。

Examples:
义1:
  • Columbus reached the Americas in 1492.
  • Columbus sailed for Spain.
  • Columbus opened the Columbian Exchange.
Notes: 开启欧陆美洲接触。

Examples:
义1:
  • Magellan led the first circumnavigation.
  • Magellan died in the Philippines.
  • Magellan's voyage proved the globe.
Notes: 首次环球航行（本人未归）。

Definition: 义1. 伊丽莎白一世（英格兰女王）
Examples:
义1:
  • Elizabeth I reigned for 45 years.
  • Elizabeth I defeated the Armada.
  • Elizabeth I's era was a golden age.
Notes: 都铎盛世， virgin queen。

Definition: 义1. 林肯（美国第 16 任总统）
Examples:
义1:
  • Lincoln abolished slavery.
  • Lincoln led the Union.
  • Lincoln was assassinated in 1865.
Notes: 美国内战、解放黑奴。

Definition: 义1. 甘地（印度独立领袖）
Examples:
义1:
  • Gandhi preached non-violence.
  • Gandhi led the salt march.
  • Gandhi won independence by peace.
Notes: 非暴力不合作运动。

Definition: 义1. 曼德拉（南非反种族隔离领袖）
Examples:
义1:
  • Mandela fought apartheid.
  • Mandela spent 27 years jailed.
  • Mandela became president in 1994.
Notes: 种族和解象征。

Definition: 义1. 丘吉尔（英国首相）
Examples:
义1:
  • Churchill led Britain in WWII.
  • Churchill rallied with his speeches.
  • Churchill warned of the Iron Curtain.
Notes: 二战领袖，冷战演说。

Definition: 义1. 罗斯福（美国总统，FDR）
Examples:
义1:
  • Roosevelt launched the New Deal.
  • Roosevelt led through the Depression.
  • Roosevelt served four terms.
Notes: 新政、二战同盟领袖。

Definition: 义1. 斯大林（苏联领导人）
Examples:
义1:
  • Stalin industrialized the USSR.
  • Stalin won WWII with huge cost.
  • Stalin's purges killed millions.
Notes: 铁腕统治，大清洗。

Definition: 义1. 列宁（苏维埃缔造者）
Examples:
义1:
  • Lenin led the 1917 Revolution.
  • Lenin founded the USSR.
  • Lenin's ideas shaped the state.
Notes: 十月革命，建苏维埃。

Definition: 义1. 孙中山（中国革命先行者）
Examples:
义1:
  • Sun Yat-sen founded the republic.
  • Sun Yat-sen led the 1911 Revolution.
  • Sun Yat-sen is 'father of the nation'.
Notes: 辛亥革命，推翻帝制。

Definition: 义1. 德川（日本幕府将军家）
Examples:
义1:
  • The Tokugawa shoguns ruled Japan.
  • Tokugawa closed the country.
  • Tokugawa kept peace for 250 years.
Notes: 江户幕府，锁国时期。

Definition: 义1. 明治（日本天皇/时代）
Examples:
义1:
  • The Meiji Restoration modernized Japan.
  • Meiji opened the country to trade.
  • Meiji built a modern army.
Notes: 明治维新，日本近代化。

Definition: 义1. 并置；把……并列以形成对照
Examples:
义1:
  • The essay juxtaposes two conflicting theories.
  • The curator juxtaposed classical and modern works.
  • Juxtaposing the data reveals a paradox.
Notes: juxtaposition (n.) 常作文学/艺术手法分析术语。
SynonymDistinction: juxtapose 把两物放一起以显差异；compare 中性比较；contrast 强调差异本身。

Examples:
义1:
  • His thesis is that institutions shape behaviour.
  • The book advances a provocative thesis.
  • She is writing her doctoral thesis.
Notes: 复数 theses；在议论文中指“中心论点”。
SynonymDistinction: thesis 指论证性主张或学位论文；argument 泛指论证；dissertation 多指博士论文。

Definition: 义1. 公理；不证自明之理
Examples:
义1:
  • Euclid built geometry from a few axioms.
  • We treated fairness as an axiom.
  • The axiom underlies the proof.
Notes: axiomatic (adj.) 自明的。
SynonymDistinction: axiom 数学/逻辑中无可辩驳的起点；maxim 道德格言；postulate 待证假设。

Definition: 义1. （用多源）交叉验证；三角定位
Examples:
义1:
  • We triangulated the finding with three methods.
  • Researchers triangulate data sources.
  • Triangulating perspectives strengthens validity.
Notes: 方法论术语，强调多证据互证。
SynonymDistinction: triangulate 特指多方法/多源互证；cross-check 一般复核。

Definition: 义1. 使可操作化（把概念转为可测指标）
Examples:
义1:
  • We operationalized 'trust' as response time.
  • The variable must be operationalized clearly.
  • Operationalizing the construct was tricky.
Notes: 社科方法论常用。
SynonymDistinction: operationalize 把抽象概念变成可观测变量；measure 仅测量。

Examples:
义1:
  • Reviewers scrutinized the methods.
  • Scrutinize the assumptions behind it.
  • The committee scrutinized every claim.
Notes: scrutiny (n.) 审查。
SynonymDistinction: scrutinize 极仔细地看；examine 一般检查；inspect 例行查验。

Definition: 义1. 伴随的；共生事物
Examples:
义1:
  • Growth brings concomitant risks.
  • Poverty and its concomitant ills.
  • There are concomitant benefits.
Notes: 正式；concomitantly (adv.)。
SynonymDistinction: concomitant 强调同时发生且相关；simultaneous 仅同时；accompanying 伴随。

Definition: 义1. 最接近的；直接的（原因）
Examples:
义1:
  • The proximate cause was a spark.
  • Distinguish proximate from root causes.
  • Proximate factors explain the event.
Notes: 对 ultimate（根本的）；proximity (n.) 邻近。
SynonymDistinction: proximate cause 直接诱因；ultimate cause 根本原因。

Definition: 义1. 综合；合成（整合为整体）
Examples:
义1:
  • The essay is a synthesis of three views.
  • Protein synthesis occurs in cells.
  • We attempted a synthesis of the data.
Notes: 对 analysis；synthesize (v.)。
SynonymDistinction: synthesis 把部分整合为新整体；analysis 拆开分析；combination 一般组合。

Definition: 义1. 反事实的（假设未发生情形）
Examples:
义1:
  • We ran a counterfactual simulation.
  • The counterfactual reveals what mattered.
  • Consider the counterfactual case.
Notes: 历史/因果推断常用。
SynonymDistinction: counterfactual 假设与事实相反以推因果；hypothetical 一般假设。

Definition: 义1. 实质性的；重大的
Examples:
义1:
  • We reached no substantive agreement.
  • A substantive change is needed.
  • The critique is substantive.
Notes: 对 procedural（程序性的）。
SynonymDistinction: substantive 触及实质内容；substantial 量大；trivial 无关紧要。

Examples:
义1:
  • We inferred intent from the actions.
  • Do not infer causation too quickly.
  • Readers infer the theme.
Notes: inference (n.)；易与 imply 混。
SynonymDistinction: infer 由证据推（接收端）；imply 暗示（发出端）。

Examples:
义1:
  • The proposition is debatable.
  • We tested the proposition empirically.
  • His central proposition fails.
Notes: propose (v.)；逻辑/哲学中“命题”。
SynonymDistinction: proposition 可真可假的陈述；claim 主张；thesis 中心论点。

Examples:
义1:
  • The test's validity is questionable.
  • We assessed construct validity.
  • Threats to validity remain.
Notes: 对 reliability（信度）；valid (adj.)。
SynonymDistinction: validity 测量是否测到该测的；reliability 结果是否稳定可复现。

Definition: 义1. 传播；散布（知识、信息）
Examples:
义1:
  • We disseminated the findings widely.
  • The journal disseminates research.
  • Funds disseminate slowly.
Notes: dissemination (n.)；比 spread 正式。
SynonymDistinction: disseminate 正式传播知识；circulate 流通；propagate 繁殖/宣传。

Definition: 义1. 明喻（用 like/as 比较）
Examples:
义1:
  • 'Brave as a lion' is a simile.
  • The simile brightens the line.
  • She used a apt simile.
Notes: 对 metaphor。
SynonymDistinction: simile 显式用 like/as；metaphor 隐式等同。

Definition: 义1. 悲情；唤起怜悯的力量
Examples:
义1:
  • The speech evoked pathos.
  • He wielded pathos skillfully.
  • Too much pathos feels manipulative.
Notes: 对 ethos/logos；pathetic (adj.) 此处指动人。
SynonymDistinction: pathos 引发同情悲悯；ethos 靠品格说服；logos 靠逻辑。

Definition: 义1. 六行诗节（十四行诗后六行）
Examples:
义1:
  • The sestet resolves the octave.
  • The sestet shifts tone.
  • Study the sestet closely.
Notes: 对 octave。
SynonymDistinction: sestet 六行收束；octave 前八行设问。

Examples:
义1:
  • The terza rima uses tercets.
  • Each tercet rhymes ABA.
  • A tercet closes the poem.
Notes: tercet 三行；如 Dante 的三韵体。
SynonymDistinction: tercet 三行诗节；triplet 三行押韵 unit。

Definition: 义1. 不谐音；刺耳之声
Examples:
义1:
  • The street was a cacophony.
  • Cacophony contrasts with euphony.
  • The cacophony broke calm.
Notes: 对 euphony（悦耳）。
SynonymDistinction: cacophony 刺耳混杂；dissonance 不和谐音；clamor 喧嚷。

Examples:
义1:
  • The line has euphony.
  • Poets seek euphony.
  • Euphony softens the mood.
Notes: 对 cacophony。
SynonymDistinction: euphony 听觉悦耳；harmony 和谐；melody 旋律。

Definition: 义1. 曲言法（以否定反表肯定）
Examples:
义1:
  • 'Not bad' is litotes for good.
  • Litotes understates for effect.
  • He used litotes to be modest.
Notes: 如 'no small feat' 意为很大成就。
SynonymDistinction: litotes 用否定弱化以强调；understatement 泛轻描淡写；hyperbole 夸大。

Definition: 义1. 交错法（ABBA 结构）
Examples:
义1:
  • 'Ask not what your country can do…' is chiasmus.
  • Chiasmus mirrors structure.
  • The speech deploys chiasmus.
Notes: 修辞格，如 'never let a fool kiss you / you kiss no fool'。
SynonymDistinction: chiasmus 结构交叉；antimetabole 词序颠倒重复。

Definition: 义1. 潜台词；言外之意
Examples:
义1:
  • The subtext is political.
  • Read the subtext between lines.
  • His calm hid a subtext of fear.
Notes: 对 text（明示）。
SynonymDistinction: subtext 未明说之意；undertone 隐含情绪/态度。

Definition: 义1. 轭式搭配（一词管两宾语，一实一虚）
Examples:
义1:
  • 'He took his vows and his leave' is zeugma.
  • Zeugma yokes two senses.
  • The poet enjoys zeugma.
Notes: 修辞格，如 'lost his wallet and his temper'。
SynonymDistinction: zeugma 一词支配不同性质宾语；syllepsis 语法上刻意不一。

Definition: 义1. 客观的（无偏见的）
Examples:
义1:
  • Strive for an objective tone.
  • The narrator is objective.
  • An objective account avoids bias.
Notes: 对 subjective；objective correlative 艾略特术语。
SynonymDistinction: objective 去个人色彩；neutral 不偏不倚；impartial 不偏袒。

Definition: 义1. 主观的（出自个人感受）
Examples:
义1:
  • Taste is subjective.
  • The essay is subjective.
  • Avoid subjective claims in data.
Notes: 对 objective。
SynonymDistinction: subjective 基于个人；personal 私人；impressionistic 印象式。

Examples:
义1:
  • An oligarchy of elites ruled.
  • The oligarchy controlled wealth.
  • Critics call it a corporate oligarchy.
Notes: oligarch (n.)；对 democracy。
SynonymDistinction: oligarchy 少数精英统治；plutocracy 富豪统治；aristocracy 贵族统治。

Examples:
义1:
  • The state became a theocracy.
  • The theocracy fused church and state.
  • Reform challenged the theocracy.
Notes: theocratic (adj.)。
SynonymDistinction: theocracy 宗教领袖执政；secular state 世俗国家；autocracy 一人统治。

Definition: 义1. 授予选举权；解放
Examples:
义1:
  • Women were enfranchised in 1920.
  • The reform enfranchised minorities.
  • Enfranchise the disenfranchised.
Notes: 对 disenfranchise；franchise (n.) 选举权。
SynonymDistinction: enfranchise 给政治投票权；empower 泛赋权；liberate 解放。

Examples:
义1:
  • They abrogated the treaty.
  • The power to abrogate is disputed.
  • Abrogate the obsolete law.
Notes: 正式，常接 treaty；对 ratify。
SynonymDistinction: abrogate 单方废约（常含违约意味）；repeal 立法废除；annul 宣告自始无效。

Examples:
义1:
  • He usurped the throne.
  • The general usurped power.
  • Usurp authority at your peril.
Notes: usurper (n.) 篡权者。
SynonymDistinction: usurp 非法夺取本属他人的权；seize 夺取；appropriate 挪用。

Definition: 义1. 剥夺（某人的）选举权
Examples:
义1:
  • The law disenfranchised thousands.
  • Felons are disenfranchised.
  • Reforms aim to enfranchise, not disenfranchise.
Notes: 对 enfranchise。
SynonymDistinction: disenfranchise 剥权；disempower 泛夺能；exclude 排斥。

Definition: 义1. 扩散；激增（尤核武）
Examples:
义1:
  • They fear nuclear proliferation.
  • Proliferation of weapons continued.
  • Curb the proliferation.
Notes: proliferate (v.)。
SynonymDistinction: proliferation 快速扩散（常带负面/安全）；spread 中性扩散；multiplication 倍增。

Definition: 义1. 可行走的；门诊的
Examples:
义1:
  • The patient is ambulatory.
  • Ambulatory care avoids admission.
  • Ambulatory surgery same-day.
Notes: 对 inpatient（住院）；ambulate (v.) 行走。
SynonymDistinction: ambulatory 能走动/门诊；outpatient 不住院就诊；mobile 可移动。

Examples:
义1:
  • She was diagnosed with anemia.
  • Anemia causes fatigue.
  • Treat the anemia with iron.
Notes: anaemic (adj.) 贫血的/虚弱的。
SynonymDistinction: anemia 红细胞/血红素不足；anaemia 同词英式拼法。

Examples:
义1:
  • He has hypertension.
  • Control hypertension with diet.
  • Hypertension risks stroke.
Notes: 对 hypotension（低血压）；hypertensive (adj.)。
SynonymDistinction: hypertension 血压过高；high blood pressure 同义俗称。

Definition: 义1. 使免疫；接种疫苗
Examples:
义1:
  • Immunize the child early.
  • They immunized the village.
  • Immunize against flu.
Notes: immunization (n.)；immune (adj.) 免疫的。
SynonymDistinction: immunize 广义获得免疫；vaccinate 接种疫苗；inoculate 接种（菌）。

Definition: 义1. 给……服镇静剂；镇静的
Examples:
义1:
  • They sedated the patient.
  • A sedate recovery room.
  • Sedate him before surgery.
Notes: sedative (n./adj.) 镇静剂；对 stimulate。
SynonymDistinction: sedate 用药镇静；calm 泛安抚；tranquilize 使镇定（常动物）。

Examples:
义1:
  • Scrub before surgery.
  • The nurse scrubbed in.
  • Surgical scrub is vital.
Notes: medical 专指术前无菌刷手。
SynonymDistinction: scrub 用力擦洗（医：刷手）；sanitize 消毒；disinfect 杀灭病原。

Definition: 义1. 传染；接触传染物
Examples:
义1:
  • Fear spread by contagion.
  • Isolate to stop contagion.
  • The contagion jumped species.
Notes: contagious (adj.)；对 contagious 强调“接触传”。
SynonymDistinction: contagion 接触传播；infection 感染；transmission 传播机制。

Examples:
义1:
  • Mosquitoes are the vector.
  • Control the vector.
  • The vector spreads dengue.
Notes: 本义向量；医：病媒（如蚊）。
SynonymDistinction: vector 携带病原的生物媒介；carrier 携带者（也可人）；transmitter 传播体。

Examples:
义1:
  • Erectile dysfunction.
  • Organ dysfunction noted.
  • Cognitive dysfunction persists.
Notes: dysfunctional (adj.) 功能失调的。
SynonymDistinction: dysfunction 功能失常；impairment 受损；disorder 紊乱/病。

Examples:
义1:
  • Exercise boosts metabolism.
  • Her metabolism slowed.
  • Drugs alter metabolism.
Notes: metabolic (adj.) 代谢的。
SynonymDistinction: metabolism 体内化学转化；breakdown 分解；processing 处理。

Examples:
义1:
  • The muscle atrophied.
  • Disuse causes atrophy.
  • Atrophy of the limb.
Notes: atrophy 肌肉/器官萎缩；对 hypertrophy（肥大）。
SynonymDistinction: atrophy 因不用而萎缩；wasting 消耗；shrinkage 缩小。

Definition: 义1. 败血症的；腐败的
Examples:
义1:
  • The wound turned septic.
